summary: Add a provider-neutral product and order search capability with a PostgreSQL tenant-scoped implementation, additive search indexes, REST contracts and conformance tests while PostgreSQL remains the system of record.

impacts.evidence: Search scope is resolved from authenticated server-side context; PostgreSQL transactions set organization/workspace scope for forced RLS and every root/child search predicate repeats both tenant keys. Client tenant identifiers are not search inputs.

Search returns minimal projections only: product descriptions, order items, customer data and tenant IDs are excluded. PostgreSQL stays authoritative and future external projections remain subject to Task 061 deletion propagation.
Additive GET/HEAD search behavior is defined for /api/v1/products and /api/v1/orders with q/filter/limit/cursor parameters and Draft 2020-12 response schemas; no existing contract is removed.
Task 026 adds no event type or event payload; search reads canonical PostgreSQL state and is not a new event contract.
Connector SDK root interfaces and provider admission are unchanged; provider-specific search APIs or external search client types do not enter the SDK.

Expand migration 000019 adds immutable text-vector helper functions plus GIN and tenant-prefixed prefix indexes over canonical product/order data; it creates no mutable search table and performs no destructive operation.

Authenticated scope is required before provider execution, RLS plus explicit tenant predicates provide defense in depth, dynamic values are parameterized, cursors and limits are validated, and responses are no-store/nosniff.
Search is read-only and introduces no approval bypass, privileged mutation path or change to Task 017 Approval Engine policy.
Search is a derived read path over existing authoritative records, persists no result state and changes no audit or immutable lineage contract.

Search is read-only; query-bound cursor fingerprints and deterministic priority/updated_at/id keyset ordering prevent an opaque cursor from being reused with a different normalized query or filter set.
No webhook or outbound network path is added; Task 063 remains responsible for durable webhook delivery.

Page sizes and query shapes are bounded, but Task 026 does not claim production latency qualification; representative EXPLAIN, latency and index-build evidence is explicitly left as deployment qualification.

The migration is additive and canonical reads remain valid if search is disabled. Production must qualify GIN/index build behavior and use the migration/Task 067 rollout path when an online index strategy is required.

Unit, API authorization, migration/static SQL, schema fixture and Task-026 audit tests cover provider neutrality, fail-closed tenant scope, cursor binding, deterministic ordering and absence of a premature external search backend.
